thread:
eva: heads-up: i ran into a weird case in sim where aggressive prefetch + demote signaling caused a backlog of inflight handoffs and spiked handoff.latency. thinking out loud about coupling prefetch admission to eviction decisions.

harry: can you describe the sequence that spikes latency? is it rehydrate traffic or the handshake churn?

eva: sequence: shard marks prefix demote -> owner kicks prefill on other nodes -> multiple owners simultaneously prefetch same prefix due to race -> ram spike and writeback flood -> shard tries forced handoff for others -> handshake queue starves -> p99 latency jumps.

mei: oof. sounds like we need a prefetch admission control that is demote-aware. maybe a token bucket keyed by prefix id + shard-level cap.

eva: exactly. proposal: introduce prefetch_admit(per-prefix) that returns allow/deny based on current shard_prefetch_slots and prefix.demote_state. when demote_state==signalled we lower priority; if shard_prefetch_slots exhausted, deny and add prefix to deferred_prefetch_queue.

cal: how to avoid starving prefetch forever? deferred queue needs fairness. suggestion: priority = min(tenant_priority, prefix.hotness) + age_bonus. we pop by highest priority every X ms.

harry: correctness: prefetch denied must not block a safe handoff. prefetch is optional optimization; handoff still needs to acquire residency token. ensure those paths are independent.

eva: agreed. we must not gate token transfers on prefetch. prefetch is speculative and should not be involved in the token ownership protocol. put it in a separate subsystem with well-defined backpressure.

mei: telemetry additions: shard.prefetch.slots_total, shard.prefetch.slots_used, prefix.prefetch.deferred_count, prefetch.admit_denied_rate, handoff.latency_p99_by_cause. ops can set alert on prefetch.admit_denied_rate rising which may indicate a hotspot.

cal: operational safety: add a safety cutoff that disables prefetching cluster-wide if memory_pressure > 80% for 2m. fallback to conservative prefetching (1 slot per shard).

ops-bot: FYI created canary plan stub: https://internal.redwood/ops/canaries/prefetch-admit-control (draft) :eyes:

harry: what about race where demote_signalled and prefetches in-flight cause a window where reads observe stale data? need invariants spelled out.

eva: invariant: reads must always consult residency token/owner. prefetch writes are local caches for read latency only. we guarantee read-after-write by blocking demote completion until owner confirms KV flush or snapshot consistent. prefetch cannot accelerate demote completion.

mei: implementational sketch: prefetch subsystem exposes callbacks: on_prefetch_start(prefix), on_prefetch_done(prefix), on_prefetch_cancel(prefix). demote path waits on owner ack that either prefetches are drained or prefix metadata indicates safe. also track prefetch.inflight_count per-prefix.

cal: pseudo: 
```
func tryPrefetch(prefix) -> bool {
  if shard.mem_pressure > 0.8 { return false }
  if shard.prefetch_slots_used >= shard.prefetch_slots_total { enqueueDeferred(prefix); return false }
  if prefix.demote_state == SIGNALLED && prefix.inflight_prefetches > 0 { // deprioritize
     if !tenantIsHighQoS(prefix.tenant) { enqueueDeferred(prefix); return false }
  }
  startPrefetch(prefix); return true
}
```

harry: tests: unit test for deferred queue ordering, integration test simulating concurrent demote + many prefetchers, and a property test that demote cannot complete while inflight_prefetches>0 unless owner explicitly permits.

eva: rollout: 1) staging sim run with trace for 72h 2) prefetch.admit control in probe mode for 24h in prod (metrics only) 3) canary 2 nodes in region with low critical tenants for 48h 4) ramp with automated rollback on lateness/backpressure gates.

ops-bot: recommended gates: handoff.latency_p99 < baseline*1.5, shard.memory_pressure < 0.75, prefetch.admit_denied_rate stable.

mei: runbook snippet: 
```
Runbook: prefetch-admit incident steps
1) flip feature flag prefetch.admit=false for region
2) inspect shard.prefetch.slots_used and prefix.prefetch.deferred_count
3) if handoff.latency high -> force cancel inflight prefetches for top affected prefixes: POST $ADMIN/prefixes/{id}/prefetch/cancel
4) if memory_pressure persists -> scale down prefetch slots cluster-wide and notify SRE
5) collect: prefetch event logs, ownership handoff traces, memory histograms
```

cal: final ask: make deferred queue pluggable so ops can change strategy (LRU, priority by tenant, FIFO) without redeploy.

eva: will make it a config in runtime with hot-reload. opening RFC follow-up with diagrams and tests: https://go.redwood/rfc/prefetch-admit-control (WIP) :rocket:

harry: LGTM. let's pair on the property tests.

eva: thanks all.
